items.q: What does Talarico mean by crony capitalism?
items.a: Gains go to those who can **buy access** to politicians, not to the people **doing the work**.

items.q: What example does he give from Texas?
items.a: With **no contribution limits**, one out-of-state billionaire gave the governor **$12 million** tied to a voucher push.

items.q: Why does replacing a politician rarely change outcomes?
items.a: Politicians are mostly **rational actors**; without new **incentives** you get **the same result**.

items.q: Which incentives does he say reward extremism?
items.a: **Big money**, **gerrymandering** and a media ecosystem that rewards outrage.

items.q: Why does he pledge to serve only two terms?
items.a: Long tenure **merges office and identity**, which pushes people toward **self-preservation**.

items.q: What does he propose for AI job disruption?
items.a: An **AI dividend** so workers **share the gains** from technology built on their ideas.
